facebook.content_angle: Hip rotation mechanics — how most club swimmers swim flat and lose stroke length and efficiency on every single lap, and the 10-degree rotation fix that adds real distance per stroke
facebook.post_text:
Most swimmers train for months and never fix the one thing costing them a body length every lap. 🌊

You're probably swimming too flat. Not because you're lazy — because no one told you that hip rotation is the engine, not a bonus.

👉 A 10-degree increase in hip rotation measurably extends stroke length and reduces frontal drag
👉 Flat swimming forces your arms to do all the work — your biggest muscles never fire properly
👉 Elite freestylers rotate through 40–50 degrees per stroke cycle — most club swimmers barely hit 20

This isn't a minor tweak. It's a mechanical shift that changes how fast you move through water permanently. 🔥

✔️ Drill focus: side-kick drill with full hip drive, 6 x 50m, focus on rolling through the hip not the shoulder
✔️ Cue: your belly button should face the lane rope — not the ceiling
✔️ Autumn training blocks are where this gets locked in before next season counts

Are you swimming flat without realising it — or has a coach already flagged your rotation?
